skill.name: gh-fix-ci
skill.description: Inspect GitHub PR checks with gh, pull failing GitHub Actions logs, summarize failure context, then create a fix plan and implement after user approval. Use when a user asks to debug or fix failing PR CI/CD checks on GitHub Actions and wants a plan + code changes; for external checks (e.g., Buildkite), only report the details URL and mark them out of scope.
skill.summary: Guide GitHub Actions CI triage, fix planning, and approved implementation.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick findings are Markdown command examples, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. I confirmed risks where the skill requests broad GitHub auth scopes, escalated sandbox access, and direct log download to a local path. No prompt injection text was found.

remediation.suggestion: Remove instructions to request sandbox_permissions=require_escalated. Ask users to approve the exact gh command and explain why network or keyring access is needed.
Document the minimum required GitHub token scopes for reading PR checks and logs. Prefer read-only access where the host supports it.
Write fetched logs only to a safe workspace or temporary path. Warn users before overwriting files or storing sensitive CI logs.

content.value_statement: Failed PR checks slow delivery when logs are hard to inspect. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through GitHub Actions triage, planning, and approved fixes.
actual_capabilities: Guides inspection of failing GitHub PR checks with the gh CLI.
Explains how to fetch GitHub Actions run metadata and logs.
Summarizes failing check names, run URLs, and relevant log snippets.
Separates GitHub Actions failures from external CI providers.
Creates a fix plan and waits for explicit approval before implementation.
Suggests rechecking CI status after changes are made.
limitations: Requires an authenticated gh CLI session for the target repository.
Only covers GitHub Actions checks in detail.
External providers such as Buildkite are reported as out of scope.
The scanned package references a helper script, but only SKILL.md is present.

use_cases.title: Debug a failing pull request
use_cases.description: Inspect failed GitHub Actions checks, collect logs, and identify the likely cause before editing code.

use_cases.title: Triage CI failures across a team
use_cases.description: Create a consistent workflow for summarizing failed checks and proposing reviewed fixes.

use_cases.title: Prepare a safe CI fix plan
use_cases.description: Turn failing workflow output into a concise plan that can be approved before code changes start.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect my PR checks
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage for a current branch pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gh-fix-ci to inspect the current branch PR checks. Summarize failures and do not change files yet.

prompt_templates.title: Review a specific PR
prompt_templates.scenario: Targeted review when the PR number or URL is known.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gh-fix-ci for PR 123. Fetch failing GitHub Actions logs, summarize the cause, and mark external checks out of scope.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a fix before editing
prompt_templates.scenario: Controlled workflow that requires approval before changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gh-fix-ci to diagnose the failing CI run, draft a short fix plan, and wait for my approval before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose and validate a fix
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for implementing and checking a CI fix.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gh-fix-ci to inspect failed checks, propose the fix, implement after approval, run relevant tests, and summarize the CI recheck steps.

output_examples.input: Inspect the current PR and explain why CI is failing.
output_examples.output: The skill reports the failing check name, the GitHub Actions run link, a concise log excerpt, and a likely cause.

output_examples.input: Create a plan to fix the failed workflow.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a short approval-ready plan with files to inspect, likely changes, and tests to run.

output_examples.input: Check whether an external provider failed.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies non-GitHub Actions checks, reports their details URL, and leaves provider-specific debugging out of scope.

best_practices: Start with read-only CI inspection before editing files.
Approve the fix plan before implementation begins.
Store CI logs carefully because they can contain sensitive data.
anti_patterns: Do not grant broad GitHub scopes when read-only access is enough.
Do not debug external CI providers through this skill.
Do not apply fixes before the failure cause is summarized.

faq.question: What does this skill help fix?
faq.answer: It helps diagnose and plan fixes for failing GitHub Actions checks on pull requests.

faq.question: Does it support Buildkite or other CI providers?
faq.answer: No. It only reports external check URLs and keeps provider-specific debugging out of scope.

faq.question: Does it change code automatically?
faq.answer: The documented workflow asks for a fix plan and explicit approval before implementation.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: An authenticated gh CLI session is required for reading PR checks and GitHub Actions logs.

faq.question: Can it summarize CI logs?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides the assistant to extract concise failure snippets from GitHub Actions logs.

faq.question: Is there a security consideration?
faq.answer: Yes. GitHub tokens and CI logs can be sensitive, so users should approve access and store logs safely.
